passages.notes: Exact UTF-8 calendar body SHA-256 including its final LF: 354bf98613b16aaf2b75195cb6aef23ed100a84c9fa0977e13a96988c7c127f7. The controlling target prints Matthiae (Matthiæ), while the former calendar Matthias was transcription damage. Pustet prints the received spelling Mathiae (Mathiæ), with one t, for the same name and inflection; this is an orthographic transformation, not a noun substitution. Every petition word and the actual Per Dominum. stop agree. The 1862 heading is on the preceding full page and the entire Secret on the next; neighboring rubrics and other prayers are excluded.

passages.locus: 1962 PDF 719, printed p. 638, no. 3469; Pustet Ratisbon 1862 PDF 614-615, printed pp. 528-529
passages.notes: Exact UTF-8 calendar body SHA-256 including its final LF: 8eccf0c2a207270588f4a2ced5b50519aa2cbf197fc9a1faa4b233210fbbe391. The target and independent Pustet pages both print providere; the proposed provenire substitution is rejected. The calendar body remains byte-identical. Target intellegentiae and historical intelligentiae are received spellings of one word, retained separately. Pustet prints a comma after intelligentiae, no comma after juventutem, a comma rather than the target semicolon after quaesumus, no comma after nos, a comma after exemplo, none after intercessione, and a comma after facere. Pustet actually stops at Per Dominum.; the target stops at Per Dominum nostrum. That contiguous longer prefix is independently printed in the separately held Pustet PDF 390, printed p. 304. The prior 1862-owned evidence had incorrectly named Tours Mame 1922 PDF 815 and its raw lines; this new chain identifies the actual Pustet pages and changes no old artifact or passage.

passages.locus: 1962 PDF 807, printed p. 726, no. 4166; Pustet Ratisbon 1862 PDF 670, printed p. 584
passages.notes: Exact UTF-8 calendar body SHA-256 including its final LF: 416fe94212bfa59cdb3a933da0ebcb77f1bcf9fd66dabc9d1d772453bb512ced. The target and independent 1862 page both read quaesumus; the former calendar quiesumus was transcription damage. The complete petition agrees word for word. Pustet prints commas after loco, tuos and meritis, none after ut or montem, and a full stop after valeamus. The target prints its own pointing. Pustet actually stops at Qui tecum vivit.; the target stops at Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate. The longer target prefix is independently printed contiguously in the separately held Pustet PDF 390, printed p. 304, Praesta oration conclusion; no words beyond the target stop are supplied.

work.description: A project-created editorial source projection containing bounded Latin prayer bodies in date-specific artifacts. It is neither an edition of a historical hand missal nor an edition of the Missale Romanum. Each artifact records the transformation rule over separate public-domain antecedent and 1962 page-image witnesses; its passages let consumers cite the projected bodies without assigning Triptych's target-controlled collation choices to the antecedent printing.
